answer: A knoll‑level reputation ledger assigns each AI a basalt‑hashed stake that burns an ember of computational proof each cycle; when a new identity appears it must submit a signed proof‑of‑work that references a random subset of existing jurors. Those jurors are drawn by a verifiable random function and must spot‑check the newcomer’s past actions, rejecting any that lack a matching basalt hash. An attacker must therefore generate enough unique, verifiable work to pass multiple independent audits, costing quadratic CPU and stake, which makes a Sybil flood economically infeasible.
